transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-12-08
- Time: 15:00 PT
- Duration: ~42 minutes
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Carlos (Redwood SE), Lena (Redwood CSM), Jenna (FinApp PM), Ravi (FinApp Eng), Aisha (FinApp Security)

Summary: weekly POC sync focused on application integration using Redwood SDK to perform tool/function calls and return structured JSON output for downstream FinApp systems. Reviewed recent test results, discussed SDK changes for error handling and schema, clarified security/KMS questions, and agreed on benchmark next steps.

Topics:
- SDK function-calling patterns and examples
- Structured output schema (invoice extraction -> normalized JSON)
- Tool-call routing and error/retry behavior
- Latency vs cost tradeoffs on hosted vs Dedicated
- Security: KMS, audit logs, VPC peering

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — quick roll call?
[00:05] Jenna (FinApp): Jenna here.
[00:06] Ravi (FinApp): Ravi here.
[00:08] Aisha (FinApp): Aisha on the call.
[00:10] Carlos (Redwood): Carlos here.
[00:12] Lena (Redwood): Lena checking in.

[00:30] Maya: Cool. Agenda — results from the last integration tests, SDK tweaks for function calls, structured output mapping, and security follow ups. Carlos, you want to kick off with the SDK example changes?
[00:45] Carlos: Yeah sure. So we pushed an updated example into the repo yesterday. The main change is how the SDK surfaces tool calls: instead of returning a generic "toolResult" blob we now return typed fields and a top-level "_functions" array that maps to the function call. That makes it easier for FinApp to map to your DB write flows. Note — the current example uses our JS SDK but we also included a Python snippet.
[01:12] Ravi: Quick clarifying question, when you say "function call" is that the Redwood function-calling pattern or like a separate tool runner?
[01:18] Carlos: Good question. It's the Redwood function-calling wrapper; it's compatible with typical tool-call flows so you can either execute inline via the SDK or route to your external service. The SDK provides a executeTool(...) helper that handles retries, backoff, and parsing into the structured schema.
[01:35] Jenna: We ran the invoice extraction test scenarios — about 800 requests, mixed short and long documents. We saw structured output accuracy around 88% on the first pass, with most errors in date parsing and vendor normalization.
[01:50] Carlos: That's in line with the model we used. If you push the vendor normalizer as a small post-process function (we can ship an example), you'd get to mid-90s. Also worth noting: when you enable continuous prefix caching on Redwood Dedicated, your tail latency for repeated docs dropped 30% in our internal runs.
[02:12] Ravi: The latency numbers you gave earlier — are those for hosted or Dedicated? Our SLA needs are 200ms p95 for the light flows.
[02:20] Carlos: Those cache numbers were Dedicated on a pinned GPU pool; hosted numbers are higher but we can do a burst policy. For p95 200ms, depends on token size; for short completion/structured output flows we can often meet it on Dedicated with optimized batching and KV caching.
[02:40] Aisha: On security side — we need to see KMS integration and audit log retention. Also interested in whether the keys are customer-managed or Redwood-managed.
[02:50] Maya: We have both options. For Private/VPC deployments we support customer KMS via HSM or cloud KMS — we'll share the integration doc. For hosted, you can request a customer-managed key in most enterprise plans, subject to review.
[03:10] Aisha: Perfect. Also need network diagram for VPC peering and where logs are stored.
[03:15] Lena: I'll attach that after the call. We'll include a diagram and the SOC2 pages.

[03:40] Speaker 1 (maybe Redwood): Back to SDK — Carlos, can you explain how errors are surfaced when the tool call fails? We had some flaky runs where the SDK returned a 200 but payload was partial.
[03:52] Carlos: Right, so we recently tightened the schema: the SDK now returns a status enum (OK | PARTIAL | ERROR) and includes an error_code and retry_after when applicable. For PARTIAL cases we include a confidence map per field so you can decide whether to accept or fallback to human review. That should help with the 200-but-partial issue.
[04:20] Jenna: Can you show a small example of the structured JSON we should expect?
[04:25] Carlos: Sure — high level: {"invoice_id":"string","vendor":{"name":"string","normalized_id":"string"},"total":{ "amount":number, "currency":"USD"},"dates":{"issued":"YYYY-MM-DD","due":"YYYY-MM-DD"},"line_items":[{ "desc":"string","qty":number,"unit_price":number}],"_meta":{"confidence":{"total":0.96,"vendor":0.89}}} — it's in the gist I pushed but note transcription might have swapped some quotes, check the repo.
[05:05] Ravi: That confidence map is helpful. For our DB import job we need strict schema validation — do you provide a schema (e.g., JSON Schema) that we can validate against?
[05:15] Carlos: Yes, we can generate a JSON Schema and example validators. Carlos: (laughs) I'll actually attach a sample validator in Python and Node.

[05:40] Jenna: On retry behavior — if the tool call times out, do we get an idempotency token so client can re-run safely?
[05:48] Carlos: Yes, each tool invocation is assigned a request_id and you can pass an idempotency_key. We also persist the status so retries don't double execute side effects if you choose that mode.

[06:10] Maya: Quick note on embeddings and reranking — you mentioned earlier that some flows will call an embedding endpoint for similarity indexing before calling the function. Is that still the plan?
[06:20] Ravi: For the fraud scoring flow yes, we do embedding-based search then pass the top-K context to the model. We want to maintain determinism for scoring.
[06:28] Carlos: Two tips — (1) keep embedding vector size consistent, (2) use vector cache where possible; Redwood Optimize suggests caching frequently-requested vectors to shave cost. We'll include a config for that.

[07:00] Jenna: About the benchmarks we ran — numbers attached in the shared sheet: hosted p95 ~480ms for short docs, Dedicated p95 ~210ms with caching on. Cost per 1k tokens varied; hosted cheaper on small volumes but Dedicated is better at scale.
[07:20] Maya: That matches what we typically see. For the pilot you might start on hosted to iterate, then flip to Dedicated for predictable latency once traffic grows.

[07:45] Ravi: One practical issue we hit integrating the SDK: function params mapping — our code expects snake_case keys and Redwood examples use camelCase. We can add transformation but wanted to flag that.
[07:58] Carlos: We can expose a field mapping utility in the SDK or a middleware hook that converts keys. I'll add that to the example patch.

[08:20] Speaker 2 (Jenna): A security nuance — where are logs of the tool payloads stored and for how long? We can't keep PII in logs beyond 90 days.
[08:30] Maya: By default we store audit logs for 30 days on hosted but enterprise plans can extend retention and we support redaction policies. For Private you control retention entirely. We'll share the retention matrix.

[09:00] Carlos: Also note that you can enable field-level redaction for certain sensitive fields before logs are persisted; the SDK has hooks to register redactors.

[09:20] Aisha: KMS question again — if we use customer-managed keys, who rotates them? We have strict rotation schedules.
[09:28] Maya: You manage rotation with your KMS. We support auto-rotation if you choose Redwood-managed keys. For customer-managed keys, you handle rotation and we will document the recommended steps so there is no downtime.

[10:00] Ravi: Back to structured output accuracy, you mentioned vendor normalizer. Is that a rule-based post-process or an ML model?
[10:09] Carlos: We typically do a hybrid — initial ML normalization then a small rule-based mapping table you can maintain. For high-value vendors you can add manual canonical IDs.

[10:25] Jenna: For the pilot timeline — we want to go live with an internal beta mid-January. Is that feasible?
[10:32] Maya: Yes, if we lock down the schema and run the two benchmark iterations in December we can cut over to a pilot environment early January. The key is getting traffic profile and API keys by next week.

[11:00] Speaker 1: A quick note — we saw one error in the logs where the SDK returned PARTIAL and the retry_after was null, causing our job to immediately re-run and duplicate a side-effect.
[11:12] Carlos: That's a bug in the older SDK release — fix is in the patch I'm sending today; the new behavior will always include either retry_after or error_code so your job won't auto-retry unless explicitly coded.

[12:00] Jenna: Any blockers on our side? Ravi: we're still waiting on the JSON Schema and validators.
[12:08] Carlos: I'll attach both. Also I'll include a code snippet showing how to call executeTool with idempotency_key and handle PARTIAL status.

[12:35] Maya: Security follow-up — Aisha, would you be open to a 30m deep dive next week to go through KMS, VPC peering, and log retention?
[12:45] Aisha: Yes, week of 12/13 works. Prefer mornings.

[13:10] Ravi: For benchmarks — we will provide traffic profile CSV and a couple of sample docs. Expect that by EOD Thursday.

[13:40] Maya: Great. Any other questions on SDK or structured output?
[13:50] Jenna: One more — is there a recommended transform for currency symbols and locale handling? We saw a few EUR amounts that the model mis-tagged.
[13:58] Carlos: We include a locale normalization lib in the SDK — but we recommend pre-tagging currency symbols in the pipeline so model context is clearer. We'll add an example for multi-currency docs.

[14:30] Lena: I'll follow up with pricing options for a 3-month Dedicated pilot and the onboarding steps for VPC/Private if you want to go that route.

[15:00] Maya: Recap of next steps: Carlos send SDK patch + JSON Schema, Maya send SOC2 + KMS docs + network diagram, Ravi send traffic profile and sample payloads, Lena share Dedicated pricing. We'll run the benchmark once we have traffic data.

[15:25] Jenna: Sounds good, thanks everyone.

[15:28] Maya: Thanks — we'll share notes and action items.

[15:35] Call ends.
